description:
Add a fallible Keyword constructor that enforces the RFC 8621 §4.1.1 keyword syntax rules.

Current state: Keyword::new(s) is infallible — accepts any String including invalid values like "has spaces" or "control\x01chars".

RFC 8621 §4.1.1 rules:
- A keyword is a case-insensitive ASCII string
- MUST NOT contain whitespace
- MUST only contain visible ASCII characters (0x21–0x7E)
- System keywords (those beginning with '$') are predefined by the spec; custom keywords MUST NOT begin with '$'
- Keywords are case-preserved on the wire but compared case-insensitively

Required addition (additive, no breaking change to existing Keyword::new):

1. pub fn Keyword::try_new(s: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, KeywordError>
   - Reject empty string
   - Reject strings containing whitespace (0x20 or 0x09)
   - Reject strings containing non-visible-ASCII (< 0x21 or > 0x7E)
   - Reject custom keywords that start with '$' (i.e. not in the known system keyword list)
     Note: the system keywords (, , , , , , , ) are valid; unknown hBcprefixed keywords should be rejected by try_new but accepted by new (for round-trip fidelity).

2. pub enum KeywordError { Empty, InvalidChar(char), ReservedPrefix }

Oracle: RFC 8621 §4.1.1 keyword ABNF.

Keep Keyword::new infallible — it is used in deserialization and changing it would break the serde impl.

Acceptance criteria:
- Keyword::try_new("valid") returns Ok
- Keyword::try_new("") returns Err(Empty)
- Keyword::try_new("has space") returns Err(InvalidChar(' '))
- Keyword::try_new("\x01ctrl") returns Err(InvalidChar('\x01'))
- Keyword::try_new("") returns Ok (system keyword)
- Keyword::try_new("") returns Err(ReservedPrefix)
- All existing keyword tests pass
- cargo test -p jmap-mail-types exits 0
- Clippy clean
title: jmap-mail-types: Add Keyword::try_new with RFC 8621 §4.1.1 validation
